claim_boundary: Finite-height normalization, logarithmic reduction, factorization, continuity, the symmetric half-weight limit at y=1, and existence of the sharp symmetric limit for every nonzero frequency are Lean-verified. Identification of that limit with the classical piecewise value remains unproved; no RH progress or novel mathematics is claimed.
verified_units: positive vertical line avoids the pole at zero
complex power equals the exponential-logarithmic kernel for y > 0
finite-height y-form equals the a = log(y) oscillatory form
the constant exp(a*c) factors exactly from the finite-height integral
the scalar and logarithmic open targets are logically equivalent
all finite scalar truncations are interval integrable
at y = 1 the raw integral equals 2*arctan(T/c)
at y = 1 the normalized symmetric limit is 1/2

open_unit.statement_shape: Identify the now-proved sharp symmetric limit value with exp(-a*c) when a > 0 and zero when a < 0.
open_unit.why_open: Integration by parts now proves sharp convergence and reduces the limit to an absolutely convergent remainder. That remainder still requires an explicit contour, Laplace, or regularized Fourier evaluation.
